governing_rule: Milestone J succeeds only if change happens without the system appearing to cause the change.
strategic_definition: Milestone J is a micro-effect milestone, not a guidance milestone. It may lightly open a small shift in how the moment is met, but may not feel directive, coaching-like, system-led, or more noticeable than the reflection itself.
proof_target: A real but minimal internal shift can occur without increasing system presence or reducing user authorship.

required_conditions.description: The current turn is reflective enough to support a small inner shift rather than a factual or utilitarian response.
A real but minimal shift is plausibly available in the current moment without requiring directive language.
The shift can remain smaller than coaching, smaller than intervention, and secondary to the main reflection.
The wording can preserve user authorship, so the shift still feels like it belongs to the user rather than the system.
The wording can remain low-claim, non-directive, and lower-presence than the surrounding response.
Neither H nor I is already sufficient to provide the needed support or continuity in this turn.

grading_rules.inadmissible: One or more required conditions fail, or the moment would need advice-like wording, or the shift would become visible as system action.
grading_rules.weak_candidate: A shift is plausible but fragile; only ultra-light J wording may be considered, and suppression is still preferred under ambiguity.
grading_rules.admissible: A real but minimal shift is plausibly supportable, and the wording can remain clearly non-directive and subordinate.
grading_rules.strong_but_still_light: A small shift is strongly supportable by the current turn, but must still remain hard to notice as a system-originated act.

hard_suppression.description: Turn is factual, utilitarian, logistical, or otherwise non-reflective.
J would need directive, advisory, or corrective wording to work.
J would increase system presence or feel like the system is doing something active.
J would reduce user authorship by making the shift feel system-suggested or system-caused.
J duplicates or competes with H already active and sufficient in the same turn.
J duplicates or competes with I already active and sufficient in the same turn.

strong_suppression.description: The main reflection already lands cleanly and fully enough without J.
Removal of J would make the response cleaner, lighter, or less system-visible.
J risks sounding like pause instruction, calming instruction, or better-response coaching.
J risks becoming the visible main act rather than a slight secondary opening.
The shift is too weak to justify extra presence.

soft_suppression.description: A shift is possible but only weakly so, and the gain may not justify even ultra-light J presence.
J would add atmosphere polishing more than real shift value.
Presence-risk or guidance-risk is not fatal but still non-zero.

suppression.default_posture: Default-off. J must be earned from the present moment and may not render simply because a shift would be nice to have.

conflict_rules.description: If H already provides enough live support, suppress J first.
If I already provides enough soft carry-over or coherence, suppress J first.
If the main reflection already contains enough opening or softening, suppress J rather than layering additional effect.
If J would make the response feel more engineered, active, or intervention-like than H or I, suppress J.

presence_rules.governing_rule: J must remain below the threshold where the system appears to be causing the shift.
presence_rules.presence_cap: J must stay harder to notice than to benefit from.
presence_rules.visibility_rule: If a user or evaluator can point to J as 'the thing that made the shift happen,' J has gone too far.

authorship_rules.governing_rule: The shift must feel like it becomes possible within the user, not imposed by the system.
authorship_rules.safe_authorship_effect: J may only make a different response slightly more available; it may not claim or direct that response.

render_permissions.ultra_light: Allowed only when a small opening is plausibly supportable and any stronger wording would risk guidance or presence drift.
render_permissions.soft: Allowed when a real micro-shift is clearly plausible and wording can remain non-directive, low-claim, and secondary.

persistence_limits.cross_turn_persistence: Disallowed. J is moment-bound and may not create a continuing micro-shift layer across turns.
persistence_limits.memory_dependency: Disallowed. J may not depend on long-window memory or carry-over to justify itself.
persistence_limits.layer_accumulation: Disallowed. J may not stack with H and I in a way that increases visible system activity.
persistence_limits.observability_cap: J may not be made more visible merely to improve measurability or demo clarity.

qa_checks: J appears only when a real but minimal shift is plausibly present in the current turn
J suppresses whenever directive wording would be needed
J suppresses whenever H or I is already sufficient
J does not increase system presence
J does not reduce user authorship
J does not sound like coaching or suggestion
J remains secondary to the main reflection
removal is preferred over refinement when mixed
J does not become a continuing layer across turns
